{"issues":[{"beatId":"b5","category":"wrong_simplification","severity":"blocking","owner":"scriptwriter","fields":["narration"],"evidence":[{"kind":"narration","quote":"A space sticks to the next word; capitals break the pattern."},{"kind":"fact","id":"fact-15","quote":"letters stay together, punctuation is split off, and a space is kept at the start of the word that follows it"},{"kind":"note","quote":"A word's token count depends on how common its pieces were in the training text, so counts vary by word, case and language."}],"problem":"Directly after the chunk rules, the beat files capitals among the pre-tokenization walls, so an engineer learns the chunker cuts on case, while the notes say the chunker keeps letters together and that capitals change the count because the capitalised pieces were rarer in training and never merged.","fix":"Replace the second half of the sentence with the real cause: capitalised pieces were rare in the training text, so the merges that build plain Paris never formed for PARIS."}]}
